1.why: verify-token only accepts the token whose SHA-256 matches the recovery bound to the current session via currentRecovery/sessionId checks.

2.why: Reset tokens are stored hashed on a session-owned recovery record, so the same code cannot be used from another user's session.

3.why: Completing MFA/password reset only marks that recovery completed and never invalidates other sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and non-https URLs are rejected, but no explicit minimum TLS version is set in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as argon2id hashes; contact is not persisted, though this is hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: There is no real email sender; responses use generic text, but the simulated delivery returns/logs the raw test token to the client.

7.why: Inputs are allowlisted (validContact/validToken/validMfaCode/strongPassword) and the UI sets textContent only, never reflecting raw HTML.

8.why: No user-controlled redirect targets exist; navigation is same-origin hash routing and fetch calls go only to /api/*.

9.why: No email HTML templates incorporate user input; client log lines are created with textContent.

10.why: API errors are generic, but testToken and testMfaCode are returned to the client and appended to the on-page logs panel.

11.why: Password hashes use argon2id and tokens are hashed, yet the MFA secret is hardcoded as 482913 in source.

12.why: No default login username/password exists, though the recovery MFA code is a fixed test value.

13.why: recovery/token/password/mfa limits call checkLimit/recordFailure and lock after repeated failures for LIMIT_WINDOW/LOCK_WINDOW.

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same generic message and does not indicate whether a contact is registered.

15.why: Tokens are randomHex(32) (64 hex chars via crypto.getRandomValues), hashed, single-use, and bound to the requesting session's recovery.
